challenge.better_approach: Leave the site alone and let spanning ticket B's scan tolerate it: that keeps N doors, which the ruling forbids. A bus verb: this site must answer with no bus. So the published tool, lazily imported, is the smallest move.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a box whose TLS identity was made under a capitalised name (Windows platform.node() can return 'AKIENDELL') keeps working: tls.has_identity skips a re-make, but the pin key on the home is home.split('.')[0] unlowered. Unmeasured; akiendell is offline 2026-11-21, so the Windows run is the falsifier's horizon.
challenge.prior_art: Ticket 5ccc7f05c932 made the same move for claude_identity (READY c9824d056); its proof shape (delete os.uname, restore in finally) is copied. validation_store.host_name's docstring already names the shared spelling.
challenge.real_collision: None terminal: RULE 1 admits a reach into system_rackmount through its published tool (inspector _published_tool, published_by_device true on the 5ccc branch).

answers.falsifier: Done when: an AST scan of cairn/devices/recovery/machines/installer/installer.py finds no call to os.uname, platform.node, platform.uname or socket.gethostname, and every host name those files read comes from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host.host_name AND with os.uname deleted, CAIRN_HOME_HOST absent from the environment, rc a scratch file and ask_text_fn recording its prompt and answering 'x', ask_cairn_home() returns status 'skipped' and its first prompt names host_name(); the scratch rc is unchanged AND with os.uname deleted and a scratch tls_dir, ask_box_identity(dry_run=True, home=host_name().upper() + '.lan') reports the home's held asks (not attaching), and ask_box_identity(dry_run=True, home='testing-rec-other-box') reports first contact with testing-rec-other-box. Wrong intent if the system device's tool cannot answer here (an import cycle, or a caller that must run before cairn is on sys.path).
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a child of spanning ticket a577fd03e307, whose measured sites were grepped over cairn/devices/system_rackmount/rackmount.py's neighbours on 2026-11-21 and whose ruling is outline 6.6.3.7 in cairn/devices/cairn/requirements/06-recovery-device.md
answers.how: Both `hostname or platform.node()...` defaults become `hostname or host_name()` with a lazy import from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host; the explicit hostname= parameter stays. ask_box_identity names the TLS identity from `me` (tls.make_identity(d, me)), and host_name() lowercases it; the dry_run tooth never makes an identity.
answers.traces_to: Outline 6.6.3.7 (the hostname comes from the system device); outline 2.3.7.1.5 (the system device's host tool is one of the client tools a device publishes, the named exception to 2.3.7; a CC by-line builds, 0.4.1); outline 17.26.1 (a published client tool lives with its device); RULE 1 (the system device's public interface is the tool it publishes); Law 1 (one answer, not N re-derivations of it).
answers.what: The installer names its box through the system device's host tool: cairn/devices/recovery/machines/installer/installer.py:134; cairn/devices/recovery/machines/installer/installer.py:182 read the host from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host and nowhere else, so this component names its box on every OS.
